title: Quarterly partner review: sprint playbook + renewal tracker
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, repeatable "sprint" style QBR playbook and renewal tracker geared for both Standard and Enterprise customers. The goal is to give CSMs and account teams a fast-to-run deck and a clear set of pre-reads, meeting scripts, and a renewal-risk tracker so meetings finish with owners and next steps.

Usage patterns (pick one):
- Lightning (20–30m): Exec touch + renewal signal check. Use for low-touch standard customers.
- Sprint (45–60m): Product + success review, 2–3 deep metrics, focused roadmap alignment. Good for growth accounts.
- Enterprise Review (75–90m): Exec + technical + procurement trackouts; includes migration/architecture appendix.

Slide-by-slide outline (single deck can include all variants; facilitator skips sections for lightning):
1) Title & quick TL;DR (1 slide)
   - Slide content: Account name, CSM, AE, current renewal date, 1-line outcome desired (e.g., "confirm renewal + identify 2 expansion plays")
   - Speaker note: Set the timeframe: "We’ll run 45 minutes; goal is alignment and clear next steps."

2) Health snapshot (1 slide)
   - KPIs: latency p50/p95 (if relevant), tokens/day, success rate, error rate, usage trends (30/90d), cost per 1k tokens trend
   - Speaker note: Highlight improvements and anomalies; keep data visual and color-coded (green/amber/red)

3) Adoption map (1–2 slides)
   - Who is using the product, what pipelines/teams, and top 3 prompts/workflows by volume
   - For Enterprise: include architecture touchpoints (VPC, KMS, data flow diagram - one small diagram)

4) Outcomes vs. plan (1 slide)
   - Original success criteria from kickoff, progress against each signal (on-track/at-risk/blocker)

5) Customer testimonials & qualitative signals (1 slide)
   - Recent support tickets, NPS snippets, case studies inside the account

6) Risk & renewal profile (1 slide)
   - Renewal status (green/amber/red), short rationale, score components: usage trend, exec engagement, financials, technical blockers, competitive signals
   - Speaker note: Use consistent rubric (0–10 scaling per component; total score 0–50, <20 high risk)

7) Proposed plays & success plan (1–2 slides)
   - Stretch expansion opportunities (embedding, dedicated capacity, private deployment) with estimated impact and owner
   - Quick wins with owners and 2-week deliverables

8) Roadmap alignment (1 slide)
   - Two items from Redwood roadmap relevant to customer and ask for product/technical feedback

9) Contract & procurement checklist (Enterprise only, 1 slide)
   - Current term, renewal window, legal contacts, procurement blockers, outstanding SOWs

10) Appendix & deep-dive slots (multiple slides)
   - Technical appendix: latency breakdown, model variants in-use, KV cache hit ratio, quantization profile recommendations
   - Data & compliance appendix: data residency, audit log links, KMS integrations status

Pre-meeting checklist (send 5 business days before):
- Update the dashboard (CSM) with last 30/90d metrics and attach CSV export
- Confirm attendees (CSM to confirm exec, tech, procurement if enterprise)
- Share 1-page pre-read highlighting: TL;DR + 3 questions we want input on
- Pre-flight legal and billing status pull (CS Ops)

Meeting facilitation script (CSM prompts):
- Opening (2m): "Thanks all, we’ll run through a quick health check and then focus on the renewal and two suggested plays. Would anyone like to add an item to the agenda?"
- Health (5m): "Top two signals we’re watching are X and Y — we’ve seen improvement/concern here."
- Risk (5m): "Based on these signals we’d classify the current renewal as <color>. To move to green we need..."
- Close (5m): "Confirm action owners and dates — I’ll follow up with a summary and calendar holds."

Renewal risk scoring rubric (example):
- Usage trend (0–10): steep drop = 0; growing = 10
- Exec engagement (0–10): no exec touch last 90d = 0; weekly exec sync = 10
- Revenue/financial health (0–10): late payments/unsecured = 0; prepaid multi-year = 10
- Technical blockers (0–10): unresolved production blockers = 0; fully integrated and signed off = 10
- Competitive/intention signals (0–10): PoC with competitor = 0; public case study = 10
Total interpret: 41–50 low risk, 26–40 medium, 0–25 high risk

Renewal tracker (text table — paste into Sheets for automation):
Columns: account-name | sku | ARR | renewal-date | current-score | last-engagement-date | next-action | owner | procurement-status | legal-status | notes
Example row (as a single-line export):
Acme Corp | Hosted API | $120,000 | 2025-08-15 | 28 | 2025-01-21 | Exec meeting scheduled 2025-02-05 | Leah Kim | Procurement: in-flight | NDA pending | SecOps asked for audit logs

Action item template (copy/paste into ticketing):
- Title: [Account] - [Action short] | Owner: [Name] | Due: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Description: [Deliverable, acceptance criteria] | Related artifact: [link]

Enterprise add-ons guidance (slides + playbook bullets):
- Bring legal & procurement into the 2nd touch if renewal within 120 days.
- Technical readiness checklist: data residency confirmed, KMS keys rotated, on-prem pilot provisioning window, performance baseline tests.
- Migration playbook: step 0 baseline, step 1 pilot, step 2 scale, step 3 cutover + rollback plan (one paragraph each)

Customer success ops: automation ideas to reduce prep time
- Dashboard template per product tier (Standard vs Enterprise) with toggles for relevant KPIs
- Scripted export that builds the renewal tracker row from billing + usage APIs
- Calendar invite templates by meeting-length (20/45/90m) pre-filled with agenda

Attachments & deliverables to include with the deck:
- CSV: last 90d usage export
- Short video (2–3 min) product highlights tailored to account
- Link to support/sr backlog filtered by account
- One-page proposal for suggested expansion with estimated savings/ROI

Retention & win-back plays (if high risk):
- 6-week "stabilize" plan: immediate SLA commitment, 1:1 engineering support hours, discount for milestone-driven renewal
- 12-week "recover": phased migration to Dedicated or Private with performance SLAs and trial pricing

Version control & follow-up cadence:
- Save each deck with a version suffix: account-yyyymmdd-v1
- After meeting: send summary within 48 hours with action items and calendar holds; create tickets in the account board within 72 hours

Notes on tone & delivery:
- For execs: keep slides data-light and outcome-focused; lead with dollar/impact statements when possible.
- For engineers/architects: include a technical appendix; offer a 1:1 follow-up deep-dive.

Appendix: rapid checklist for legal/procurement (one pager you can attach)
- Confirm final contract owner + email
- Outstanding statements of work (SOW) and change orders list
- Renewal pricing currently applied vs list price and any discounts documented
- If customer requires audit/compliance paperwork, attach current certs and timeline to deliver

Feedback loop (how to update this template):
- Add any new deck components to the product-feedback thread in #cs-qbr-feedback Slack and tag the owner.
- Recommend monthly sync between CS leads to review templates after large renewals (>= $250k).

Quick templates (copy-paste snippets):
- Email subject for pre-read: "Pre-read: QBR — [Account] — [Date] (15m)"
- Pre-read opener: "Attached is a 1-page snapshot; please confirm any additional items to discuss. Our goal is to secure alignment on the renewal and confirm next steps."

---
Author notes: This document is intentionally structured to be a lightweight, reusable sprint-playbook for QBRs across tiered accounts. The tracker is designed to be machine-friendly (single line rows for quick pastes) and the rubric yields a single numeric signal for prioritization queues. Please add any account-specific fields (e.g., SSO status, P0 incidents) as needed when copying to Sheets.
